why: The same table's OTHER direction, which the missing-property rule does not cover. Claiming a tool the block's own union does not declare — a sibling's verb, or a name nothing registers — is an EXCESS property on a fresh object literal, so an over-claiming predicate is as unwritable as an under-claiming one. It rides a different block from its twin on purpose: two fixtures that shared a subject would prove one table exact rather than the shape of every table.

edits.replace: claims<InboxResult>({ noteDrop: true, noteFault: true, setPriority: true })
